summary.text: An 86-year-old female presented with a 6 months history of a non-painful lesion of the left lower gingiva. Examination showed a firm mandibular gingival swelling with a blunt, pebbly cobble-stone surface on the buccal and lingual aspects of the premolar-molar region, colored like the surrounding mucosa with red-white areas, with no palpable draining lymph nodes. Preoperative radiographic evaluation showed no evidence of bone involvement.

An incisional biopsy specimen measuring 1.5 × 1 cm down to bone was examined microscopically. The lesion showed proliferation of well-differentiated stratified squamous epithelium forming endophytic branching networks with keratin-filled clefts and crypts, characteristic burrowing architecture, cyst-like sinuses (with keratin-debris tracts in the Fig. 2 caption), and neoplastic islands with minimal atypia and mitosis and stromal reaction. A diagnosis of oral carcinoma cuniculatum, a variant of OSCC, was made.

Because the case showed no bone invasion, the surgical decision was a wide excision. Neck dissection was not carried out as there was no clinical indication. The authors note that management was hard because of the patient age.
